sections.title: Requirements and risk
sections.applicabilityHint: Applies when the change adds or changes a requirement, a hazard or a risk control.

items.text: Is every changed or new software requirement unambiguous, testable and traceable to a user need or system requirement?
Are the software requirements consistent with each other and free of conflicts with existing requirements?
Is the software safety classification of the affected items recorded and still justified by the change?
Are new or changed hazards, hazardous situations and risk controls identified and recorded in the risk management file?
Is each risk control implemented in software defined as a requirement and traced to its verification?

sections.title: Design, architecture and SOUP
sections.applicabilityHint: Applies when the change affects the software architecture, a detailed design or a third-party component.

items.text: Does the architecture show how the affected software items and their interfaces satisfy the requirements?
Are the interfaces between software items and to external systems specified completely and consistently?
Is the segregation of items of different safety classifications still effective after the change?
For each new or changed third-party component (SOUP): are its purpose, version, functional and performance needs and known anomalies recorded and evaluated?
Does the detailed design of each changed unit describe its behavior well enough to implement and verify it?

sections.title: Implementation
sections.applicabilityHint: Applies to every change of source code.

items.text: Does the code implement the design and requirements it is traced to, and nothing beyond them?
Does the code follow the coding standard of the project, and are deviations justified?
Are errors, invalid inputs and resource limits handled in a way that matches the design?
Are the results of static analysis and compiler warnings reviewed, and any suppression justified?
Have the units that were changed been reviewed against the acceptance criteria that were set for them?

sections.title: Verification
sections.applicabilityHint: Applies when tests or other verification evidence are added or changed.

items.text: Does every changed requirement have verification that is traced to it and that covers its acceptance criteria?
Are unit, integration and system test cases specific about inputs, expected results and pass criteria?
Are the test results recorded, with the version of the software and the environment they were obtained with?
Are failed, blocked or skipped tests and anomalies analyzed, and are their resolutions recorded?
Was regression verification chosen to cover the areas that the change can affect?

sections.title: Configuration management
sections.applicabilityHint: Applies to every change; some checks may not apply to a documentation-only change.

items.text: Are all changed items, including documents and third-party components, identified and under version control?
Is the change traceable to a change request or problem report, with its approval recorded?
Is the impact of the change on other items and on the released software analyzed and recorded?
Can the build be reproduced from the identified versions of the sources and tools?

sections.title: Documentation
sections.applicabilityHint: Applies when user-facing behavior, interfaces or the development records change.

items.text: Are the software development plan and the records that the change affects updated?
Are the user documentation, labeling and instructions for use updated for the changed behavior?
Do the traceability records connect needs, requirements, design, implementation and verification for the change?
Are the review records complete: who reviewed what, the findings, and how each finding was resolved?
